messages:
anya: Quick follow-up on streaming hedging. We have been treating hedges as a last-resort in the gateway, but a few product routes want lower p95 even if it complicates reconstruction. Need a defensible contract for when gateway can merge/switch streams.

matt: TLDR: two orthogonal axes — hedging semantics (none, switch-only, merge-capable) and side-effect policy (no-side-effect, idempotent, nondurable). Default should be 'switch-only' for safety.

diego: Clarify switch-only: gateway abandons primary and begins new stream from scratch; client sees no duplicate tokens but may see a rewind. That requires upstream support for resume tokens or deterministic restart point.

zoe: Right — propose embedding `X-RI-Resume-Token` in stream frames (opaque base64). Upstream returns token frames periodically. Gateway can then request resume from second upstream using that token. If upstream refuses, gateway fails.

anya: Nice. What about speculative merge where pieces from two upstreams are interleaved? That's messy for billing and correctness.

matt: Speculative merge only for routes with idempotent, read-only workloads (embeddings, completions for assistant-only sessions) and only when upstream advertises `X-RI-Mergeable: true`. Merge requires fragment ids and sequence anchors.

diego: I propose headers/frames: `X-RI-Fragment-Id`, `X-RI-Fragment-SeqStart`, `X-RI-Fragment-SeqEnd`, and `X-RI-Fragment-Checksum`. Gateway will verify checksums and only accept non-overlapping fragments.

zoe: Also need dedupe window semantics. If two upstreams return same tokens (retry overlap) we should drop duplicates based on checksum+sequence. Define a short dedupe TTL (default 30s) per idempotency key.

anya: Edge config example in route.yaml: ```
route: /v1/live
  streaming:
    hedging:
      allowed: true
      mode: switch_only #|mergeable
      max_parallel: 1
      dedupe_ttl_seconds: 30
    side_effects: idempotent
```

matt: Observability: when gateway performs a switch or merge, emit structured events: `switch_initiated`, `resume_failed`, `merge_fragment_accepted`, `merge_checksum_mismatch`. Console should show a mini-timeline with fragment provenance.

diego: For traces we attach `rw.gateway.attempt` with attempt_id and keep upstream spans as children. When merge happens we mark attempt that won finalization with `rw.gateway.finalized_attempt`. Billing tools will sum attempted token counts but Console will show normalized tokens consumed.

zoe: Security: don't let client provide arbitrary resume keys. Gateway will synthesize internal resume pointers and map them to opaque upstream tokens. Upstream tokens are never exposed to client.

anya: Operational note: most community model variants won't implement fragment headers. So default to `hedging.allowed=false` for public hosted routes. Dedicated customers can opt-in and we whitelist upstreams by name.

matt: Corner case: long-lived streaming where upstream sends intermittent heartbeats. If primary stalls but still sends heartbeat, should we switch? Define a stall threshold and a soft-deadline check that factors in progress (seq advances) not heartbeats.

diego: Agreed. Use progress-based deadline: if no seq advancement for X ms and no resume token progress for Y ms, consider stalled. Heartbeat only toggles liveness, not progress.

ci-bot: CI: hedging-state-machine PR 5082 passed unit tests; integration pipelines are queued (jenkins/5082) :white_check_mark:

zoe: Action items: (1) add `resume-token` and `fragment` header/frame spec to routing RFC, (2) define default dedupe TTL and stall thresholds, (3) Console UX mock for fragment timelines, (4) whitelist policy for Dedicated. I'll start the mock.

anya: I'll own the RFC updates and coordinate with infra to generate synthetic tokens for client mapping.

matt: I'll document invariant: gateway must never surface internal upstream tokens to clients and must avoid making side-effectful retries for non-idempotent routes.

diego: I'll draft a small test harness that simulates partial streams + mergeable fragments.

anya: Thanks team :rocket:
